sprintGoal: Add an opt-in agentic graph-reasoning loop to memclaw_recall, inspired by MRAgent's typed multi-tool query-time reasoning (Ji-shuo/MRAgent): instead of always doing one fixed hybrid-scored retrieval + fixed <=2-hop graph boost, an explicit reasoning_mode=true param lets the LLM pick from typed graph-query tools (by keyword, by graph-context, by time range, by entity links) across up to 3 turns to better answer relational/temporal questions. Must be strictly additive: default reasoning_mode=false path is byte-identical to today's call sequence (no latency regression on the documented 23ms p50 benchmark), and reasoning_mode=true only adds boosted ids on top of the existing single-pass result, never replaces it.

workItems.objective: Create graph_query_tools.py with typed async tool wrappers around four already-tested retrieval primitives, each returning (memory_ids, entity_ids, note) so the reasoning loop can call them uniformly.
acceptanceCriteria: New file core-api/src/core_api/services/graph_query_tools.py defines query_by_keyword, query_by_graph_context, query_by_time_range, query_by_entity_links as async functions with a consistent (memory_ids: list[str], entity_ids: list[str], note: str) return shape
query_by_keyword wraps extract_entity_tokens() + storage_client.fts_search_entities() (storage_client.py:1218) — no new SQL, no new storage endpoint
query_by_graph_context wraps memory_service.expand_graph() (memory_service.py:2594), which itself calls storage_client.expand_graph() (storage_client.py:1221)

query_by_time_range wraps memory_service._extract_temporal_date_range() (memory_service.py:3007-3060) to parse the date window, then storage_client.list_memories_by_filters() (storage_client.py:1039) with created_after/created_before set
query_by_entity_links wraps storage_client.get_memory_ids_by_entity_ids() (storage_client.py:1301)
Each wrapper catches its own exceptions and returns ([], [], '<tool>: error - <msg>') rather than raising, so a single bad tool call cannot abort the loop
A TOOL_SPECS list/dict describing each tool's name, one-line description, and expected args (for building the LLM tool-selection prompt in RL-02) is exported from this module
ruff check passes on the new file

reasons: Pure wrapper module — no changes to any existing function
New file only, nothing imports it yet so it has zero effect on the running system

workItems.objective: Create graph_reasoning_loop.py implementing run_reasoning_loop(): a bounded, never-raising multi-turn loop that asks the LLM to pick a typed tool each turn (via complete_json), executes it, and accumulates boosted memory ids and a boost factor.
acceptanceCriteria: New file core-api/src/core_api/services/graph_reasoning_loop.py defines async def run_reasoning_loop(query: str, tenant_id: str, config, seed_entity_ids: list[str]) -> tuple[set[str], float, list[dict]] returning (boosted_memory_ids, boost_factor, trace)

New constants GRAPH_REASONING_MAX_ITERATIONS = 3, GRAPH_REASONING_STEP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, GRAPH_REASONING_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS defined in this module (not per-org configurable in v1, per plan scope decision)

Each turn builds a prompt listing TOOL_SPECS from graph_query_tools.py plus a 'done' option, calls LLMProvider.complete_json(prompt, response_schema={'tool': str, 'args': dict}) via call_with_fallback (common/llm/retry.py), same pattern recall_service.summarize_memories() already uses
Loop stops when the model returns tool='done', when GRAPH_REASONING_MAX_ITERATIONS is reached, or when the total-timeout asyncio.wait_for fires

Any exception raised by the LLM call, JSON parsing, or a tool wrapper is caught inside the loop; the function returns whatever (boosted_memory_ids, boost_factor, trace) has been accumulated so far and never propagates the exception to the caller
trace is a list of {turn, tool, args, result_count} dicts usable for diagnostic mode
Unit-testable in isolation: run_reasoning_loop accepts an injected llm/provider argument (or resolves via the same seam call_with_fallback uses) so tests can supply a scripted provider

reasons: Genuinely new orchestration pattern — no existing multi-turn tool-calling loop in-repo to copy
Must never raise or hang, since it will sit in the recall path once wired in RL-03 — bounded by both iteration count and asyncio.wait_for timeout
New file only in this task; still has zero effect on production until RL-03 wires it in

payload.fallback_note: _entity_boost_pipeline's existing fallback-on-failure pattern in memory_service.py is the model for 'never raise, return partial results'

workItems.objective: Wire an opt-in reasoning_mode: bool = False parameter through mcp_server.memclaw_recall -> recall_service.recall() -> memory_service.search_memories(), additive-only: when true and graph_expand is true, run_reasoning_loop() runs after the existing _entity_boost_pipeline() call and its results are unioned in, never substituted.
acceptanceCriteria: memclaw_recall MCP tool handler in mcp_server.py accepts reasoning_mode: bool = False and passes it through to recall_service.recall()
recall_service.recall() signature gains reasoning_mode: bool = False and forwards it to search_memories()

When reasoning_mode is True but graph_expand is False, the reasoning loop is skipped (mirrors existing graph_expand gating for the fixed-hop boost)
